findings.how: Round 1 (c9a4638): windows.ts appMenuTemplate() returns null on Windows and Linux, and setUpAppChrome() calls Menu.setApplicationMenu(null) there. main.ts calls it on every OS, before any window opens. Real Electron under Xvfb after the fix: getApplicationMenu() is null, Ctrl+Q no longer quits, and Ctrl+Shift+I, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+W, F11 and the Alt bar are gone. Chromium still handles Ctrl+A/X/C/V/Z in fields. Round 2 (4c389cc), for the verifier's accessibility point: I kept the menu null and gave zoom back to the settings window only. createHomeWindow(os) calls zoomByKeys(win.webContents, os), which handles before-input-event on Windows and Linux. The mapping is in a new pure function, zoomLevelFor(os, input, level). On key down with Ctrl held (and no Alt, so no AltGr, and no Meta): Ctrl+= or Ctrl++ (Shift+= on a US keyboard, the + key on other layouts, numpad +) adds 0.5, Ctrl+- (and numpad -) takes 0.5 off, and Ctrl+0 resets. Each step calls preventDefault. The level stays between ZOOM.min -3 and ZOOM.max 5, which is 58% to 249%: WCAG's 200% text is level 3.8. macOS gets no zoom, as on the base (its menu has no View menu). The command and prompt windows don't zoom. A scratch Electron probe (zoomshare.cjs) showed Chromium keeps a file:// page's zoom to its own window: setting window A to 1.5 left window B at 0. main.ts passes platform.os to createHomeWindow. Real app under Xvfb with XTest keys on the focused settings window (scratchpad/shell/r2/zoom-keys.mjs): Ctrl+= 0.5, Ctrl+Shift+= 1, Ctrl+KP_Add 1.5, Ctrl+- 1, Ctrl+KP_Subtract 0.5, Ctrl+0 0, then seven Ctrl+- steps stop at -3, Ctrl+0 0, and Ctrl+A leaves it at 0. The page's keydown listener saw only the modifiers and Ctrl+a, never a zoom key. The handle stayed at 0. The verifier's zoomq-probe.mjs on the fix build now gives zoomAfterCtrlMinus -0.5 and zoomAfterCtrlEqual 0.5, the same as the base (it read 0 and 0 before this round), with menu null and exitedAfterCtrlQ false.

findings.how: Unchanged from round 1. The menu part is the same change as #243. In a packaged build, setUpAppChrome registers app.on('web-contents-created') with lockDevTools, which closes DevTools on 'devtools-opened'. That covers every page, including those of ask.ts, overlay.ts, handle.ts, voice.ts and desk/view.ts. Development runs keep DevTools. In real Electron 44, devtools-lock-probe.mjs gave {opened:1, stillOpen:false}, and chrome-probe.mjs showed Ctrl+Shift+I opens nothing. I did not add the optional before-quit handler: with no menu, nothing on Windows or Linux calls app.quit() outside quitEmber, and on macOS such a handler would also catch the Dock's Quit and logout, which lifecycle's session-end handling covers and I can't check here.

findings.how: Round 1 (a8e1c4d): mac-bundle.mjs signs with --options runtime and --entitlements. ENTITLEMENTS are allow-jit and allow-unsigned-executable-memory (V8), disable-library-validation (an ad hoc signature has no team ID), device.audio-input and automation.apple-events. After signing it reads back the runtime flag and the entitlements, and it fails closed if the flag is missing or if allow-dyld-environment-variables or get-task-allow is present. The fuses.mjs RunAsNode comment now states the TCC caveat. Round 2 (232ecef), for the verifier's CI point: the macOS runner logs say 'System Integrity Protection status: disabled.' (cilogs/ci133, 2 matches). In both packaged checks (macos and macos-x64), the `codesign --display | grep runtime` line stays unconditional. The DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES probe now runs only when `[[ "$(csrutil status 2>&1)" == *"status: enabled"* ]]`. Otherwise the step prints `::notice::SIP is off on this runner: the DYLD_* check can't prove anything here`. I used a [[ ]] string test rather than `csrutil | grep -q`, so GitHub's `bash -eo pipefail` can't turn an early grep exit into a false result. Checked by parsing the YAML, running `bash -n` on both run blocks, and running the SIP block with stub csrutil (on/off) and stub binaries (one honours DYLD, one ignores it). SIP on: the ignoring binary passes and the honouring one fails the step (exit 134). SIP off: the notice prints and the step goes on. So the DYLD behaviour is unproven in CI on the hosted runners: there only the runtime flag is checked. The docs lines the verifier asked for are in forDocs (docs/** belongs to the docs package). Still left, as in round 1: RunAsNode stays on. The AX sidecar host, the Linux desk helper, the commands' job host, SSH askpass and the WSL launcher all run Ember's binary with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE. So on macOS, a program running as the user can start Ember's binary as Node and, when launchd starts it, act with Ember's Accessibility and Screen Recording grants. Proposal: move those helpers to utilityProcess.fork (stdio pipes) or a small separately signed Node helper, then set RunAsNode:false and drop CI's 'node mode kept' checks. That spans the perception, cmdcore/commands, remote and platform packages. Library validation stays off until Ember has a Developer ID team.

findings.how: Round 1 (e149eac): setUpAppChrome sets nativeTheme.themeSource = 'dark' on every OS before any window opens. That makes Windows title bars and Electron menus dark, and macOS title bars, menus and NSAlert dialogs. Round 2 (272fbbe), for the verifier's must-fix: themeSource doesn't reach GTK. I reproduced it on the round-1 build with the verifier's variant-probe.mjs: both Ember windows had variant=None. createHomeWindow, createCommandWindow and createPromptWindow now pass darkTheme: true (one line each; Electron reads it on Linux only). After a rebuild, the same probe shows the settings window ('Ember') with variant=b'dark'. The other window, still None, is the handle (mapped by getNativeWindowHandle in scratchpad/shell/r2/app-variant.mjs). It is frameless and has no title bar. The command and prompt windows aren't opened at start, so I bundled windows.ts on its own with esbuild and made all three windows with its factories in Electron 44 (scratchpad/shell/r2/winmod/factories.cjs). Settings 'Ember', command 'Ember commands' and prompt 'Ember' all read _GTK_THEME_VARIANT=b'dark'. For the should-fix, the setUpAppChrome JSDoc and DESIGN.md's Colour line now say only what is true: title bars are dark on Windows, macOS and GNOME, native menus and dialogs on macOS, and menus on Windows. On Linux, menus and dialogs follow the GTK theme, and Windows' message boxes (the quit question) stay light. The main.ts comment now says 'the dark native theme', not 'dark native chrome'. Marked partial because part of the finding's scenario can't be met by themeSource or darkTheme. The GTK quit question and Menu.popup menu on Linux stay light under a light GTK theme (verifier's dark.png). The Windows quit question is a TaskDialog, which has no dark mode. Proposals, both beyond this package: on Linux, set GTK_THEME=Adwaita:dark in the launchers (/usr/bin/ember, the AppImage's AppRun), since GTK is initialised before main.js runs; on Windows, a dark quit question would need Ember to draw its own dialog, which is a design task.

DEVELOPING.md, a caveat by the macOS fuses bullet (~line 876), with the node-mode wording at ~line 328 (Linux) and ~line 580 (Windows, 'Node mode kept for the accessibility host') naming every helper: RunAsNode stays on because Ember's helpers run its binary as plain Node: the accessibility host, the desk helper on Linux, the commands' job host, SSH's askpass helper and the WSL launcher. So any program running as the user can start Ember's binary as Node with a script of its own. On macOS, if it is started so that macOS holds Ember responsible for it (by launchd, say), it acts with Ember's Accessibility and Screen Recording grants. This stays so until the helpers leave ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE (review #177). The hardened runtime closes the DYLD_* and debugger ways in.

DEVELOPING.md, where CI's macOS packaged checks are described: CI reads the hardened-runtime flag on Ember.app's signature, and tries DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES only where SIP is on. The hosted macOS runners report SIP off, so there it leaves a notice, and the DYLD behaviour is unproven in CI.

verifierProblems.what: On Linux, the platform the finding names for GNOME title bars, nativeTheme.themeSource = 'dark' changes nothing you can see. A real-Electron probe on the fix build (relfix-verify/shell/variant-probe.mjs with xprops2.py) shows Ember's windows have no _GTK_THEME_VARIANT, the same as on the base, and that X property is what Mutter reads to draw a dark title bar. A scratch Electron 44 test (relfix-verify/shell/dark/main.cjs) shows a window built with darkTheme: true gets _GTK_THEME_VARIANT=dark, while one with only themeSource 'dark' gets none. A screenshot with themeSource 'dark' (relfix-verify/shell/dark/dark.png) shows the GTK quit question ('Ember is still working on 3 tasks.') and a Menu.popup menu both still light. So on RHEL 8 GNOME with the default light Adwaita theme, the settings, command and prompt windows keep light title bars around a near-black page. The report still marks #245 'fixed … on every OS'.
verifierProblems.fix: In app/main/windows.ts, add `darkTheme: true` to the BrowserWindow options of createHomeWindow, createCommandWindow and createPromptWindow. Electron documents this option for Linux only and ignores it on Windows and macOS. It is 3 one-line shared hunks. Add a unit test that the three factories pass darkTheme (with an electron mock that records options), and re-run the X11 property check, which should show variant=b'dark' on the 'Ember' and 'Ember commands' windows.

verifierProblems.what: Two texts claim more than the code does. docs/DESIGN.md's new Colour line says 'title bars, native menus and dialogs are dark whatever the system's appearance', and the setUpAppChrome JSDoc says the same. On Linux, themeSource reaches none of these: the GTK message box and the Menu.popup menu stay light (dark.png). On Windows, dialog.showMessageBox is a TaskDialog, which has no dark mode, so the quit question will stay light there too. Only macOS (NSAlert and menus) and the Windows title bars and Chromium-drawn menus follow themeSource.
verifierProblems.fix: Reword the DESIGN.md line and the JSDoc to what is true. For example: 'Ember is dark only: title bars are dark on every OS, and native menus and dialogs are dark on macOS. On Linux they follow the GTK theme, and Windows message boxes stay light.' Adjust it once darkTheme is in for Linux title bars.

verifierProblems.what: This is an accessibility regression on Linux and Windows that the finding itself warned about ('zoom is a useful accessibility feature the default menu accidentally provides'; its suggested fix offered a menu that keeps Edit and zoom). I ran a real-Electron probe under Xvfb (relfix-verify/shell/zoomq-probe.mjs) with the settings window focused. On the base, Ctrl+- gives zoom level -0.5 and Ctrl+Shift+= gives +0.5. On the fix build, both stay at 0, and Ctrl+0 is gone too. Settings no longer has any way to enlarge text on Linux or Windows. The css package's #57 adds no zoom. The report's reason, that a zoom-only menu would bring back the Alt bar, is true for a menu, but zoom doesn't need one.
verifierProblems.fix: Keep the menu null. Restore zoom on the settings window only: the command and prompt windows are fixed size and clip when zoomed (#57). In createHomeWindow, or in setUpAppChrome on Windows and Linux, handle `webContents.on('before-input-event')`. Map Ctrl+= and Ctrl++ to +0.5, Ctrl+- to -0.5 and Ctrl+0 to reset, clamp the level (for example to -3..3), and call preventDefault. Put the key-to-zoom mapping in an exported pure function with unit tests. If the lead decides to drop zoom instead, the report must say that Ctrl+-/+/0 zoom is gone on Windows and Linux, and #57 must be told.

verifierProblems.what: The new CI line `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES=/nonexistent/... ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$exe" -e 'process.exit(0)'` assumes macOS drops DYLD_* for a binary under the hardened runtime. The repo's own macos-15 (arm64) runner logs say 'System Integrity Protection status: disabled.' (scratchpad/cilogs/ci133/'2_macOS (...)'.txt and scratchpad/ci/run12x.log). With SIP off, AMFI's dyld policy may honour DYLD_* (dyld's own fallback treats only SIP-on as restricted). In that case dyld aborts on the missing library and the packaged check fails for a reason that has nothing to do with Ember. If dyld does pass the line, it proves nothing about users' Macs either.
verifierProblems.fix: In both macOS packaged-check steps (ci.yml ~line 541 and ~722), keep the `codesign --display … | grep runtime` line unconditional. Run the DYLD probe only when `csrutil status | grep -q 'status: enabled'` succeeds. Otherwise print `::notice::SIP is off on this runner: the DYLD_* check can't prove anything here`. Say in the report that the DYLD behaviour is unproven in CI.

verifierProblems.what: The reviewer's fix asks to 'state the TCC caveat in the docs' until RunAsNode can go off. Only the fuses.mjs comment was changed. docs/DEVELOPING.md §11.5 (line 878) still says the bundle is 'signed ad hoc last and verified', with no word of the hardened runtime or its entitlements. Lines 328 and 580 still describe node mode as harmless ('Node mode kept for the accessibility host'), with no caveat that any program the user runs can start Ember's binary as Node and use Ember's Accessibility and Screen Recording grants. The fix agent's report is cut off after 'ciOnly', so I can't see whether this went to the docs package.
verifierProblems.fix: Add to the report's forDocs for the docs package, which owns docs/**: (1) DEVELOPING.md line 878 bullet: 'signs the whole bundle ad hoc under the hardened runtime with mac-bundle.mjs ENTITLEMENTS (JIT, unsigned executable memory, library validation off, microphone, Apple events), then reads back the runtime flag and the entitlements'; (2) a short caveat near the fuses text: RunAsNode stays on for the helpers, so on macOS a program running as the user can start Ember's binary as Node and act with Ember's TCC grants, until the helpers leave ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE (review #177).
